items.name: addGoApp
items.description: Adds a Go application to the application model. The Go toolchain must be available on the PATH.
items.remarks:
This method executes the Go application using `go run .`. The Go toolchain resolves the
entry point from the package in `appDirectory`.
Go applications automatically have VS Code debugging support enabled via Delve.
Use `WithModTidy``1`, `WithModVendor``1`, or `WithModDownload``1`
to manage module dependencies before startup, and `WithVetTool``1` to run static analysis.
Use `WithAppArgs``1` to pass runtime program arguments, and
`WithDelveServer``1` to enable remote debugging via a headless Delve server.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the resource.

parameters.name: appDirectory
parameters.description: The path to the directory that acts as both the Go module root (where `go.mod` lives) and the Docker build context for `aspire publish`.

parameters.name: packagePath
parameters.description: The Go package to run or build, relative to `appDirectory`. Defaults to `"."` (the module root itself). Use a sub-path such as `"./cmd/server"` when the main package is not at the module root (e.g. `api/cmd/server/main.go` with `api/go.mod`). This value is passed to `go run`, `dlv debug`, and `go build` consistently.

parameters.name: buildTags
parameters.description: Optional build tags passed to the compiler via `-tags` (e.g. `"netgo"`, `"integration"`).

parameters.name: ldFlags
parameters.description: Optional linker flags passed via `-ldflags` (e.g. `"-X main.version=1.0.0"`).

parameters.name: gcFlags
parameters.description: Optional compiler flags passed via `-gcflags` (e.g. `"all=-N -l"` to disable optimisations for Delve).

parameters.name: raceDetector
parameters.description: When `true`, enables the Go race detector by passing `-race` to `go run`.

items.name: withDelveServer
items.description: Starts a configurable headless Delve debug server so that DAP-compatible clients can attach remotely. The application is launched with `dlv debug` instead of `go run`. Delve must be available on the PATH.
items.remarks:
The server listens on `127.0.0.1` and accepts a single debugger client by default.
Set `AcceptMultiClient` to `true` only when
multiple clients or reconnections are required.

items.name: withGoPrivate
items.description: Configures private Go module authentication for publish-time Dockerfile generation.
items.remarks:
Only affects the generated Dockerfile — has no effect in run mode, where the local
Go toolchain picks up credentials from the developer's own `~/.netrc` or git
credential helper.
The generated build stage writes a temporary `.netrc` file from the username
build-arg and the token secret, runs `go mod download`, then removes the file —
all in a single layer so credentials never persist in the image.

parameters.name: privatePatterns
parameters.description: One or more module path patterns that should bypass the public proxy and checksum database, e.g. `"*.mycompany.com"` or `"github.com/myorg"`. Passed verbatim to `GOPRIVATE`, which implicitly covers `GONOSUMCHECK` and `GONOPROXY`.

parameters.name: authHost
parameters.description: The Git host that requires authentication, e.g. `"github.com"`.

parameters.name: usernameArgName
parameters.description: The Docker build-arg name for the Git username. Defaults to `"GIT_USER"`. Pass it at build time with `--build-arg GIT_USER=myuser`.

parameters.name: tokenSecretId
parameters.description: The BuildKit secret ID for the Git access token. Defaults to `"gittoken"`. Pass it at build time with `--secret id=gittoken,src=/path/to/token`.

items.name: GoAppResource
items.description: Represents a Go application resource in the distributed application model.
items.remarks:
This resource allows Go applications to run as part of a distributed application. The resource
manages the Go toolchain, working directory, and lifecycle of the Go application.
Go applications can expose HTTP endpoints, communicate with other services, and participate
in service discovery like other Aspire resources. They support automatic OpenTelemetry
instrumentation when configured with the appropriate Go packages.

items.name: DelveServerOptions
items.description: Configures the headless Delve debug server used for remote debugging of a Go application.
items.remarks:
The server listens on the loopback interface. By default, it accepts a single debugger client
and relies on Delve's default same-user connection policy.
Set `AcceptMultiClient` only when the server must remain available after a debugger
disconnects or when multiple debugger clients need to attach.

fields.name: Port
fields.description: Gets the TCP port on which Delve listens. The default is `2345`.

fields.name: AcceptMultiClient
fields.description: Gets a value indicating whether Delve accepts multiple debugger clients. The default is `false`.

fields.name: OnlySameUser
fields.description: Gets a value indicating whether Delve allows connections only from the same operating system user. When `null`, Delve's default same-user policy is used.

fields.name: ContinueOnStart
fields.description: Gets a value indicating whether Delve continues the application immediately after startup. The default is `false`.

fields.name: Log
fields.description: Gets a value indicating whether Delve server logging is enabled. The default is `false`.

fields.name: LogOutput
fields.description: Gets the Delve logging components enabled when `Log` is `true`. When `null` or empty, Delve uses its default logging components.
